patches.old: We report a separation between category-sensitive localization and relational object selection in evaluated CLIP pipelines. A map that highlights a category need not identify the intended instance among objects of that category. We analyze saved COCO experiments with a frozen ViT-B/16, ordinary and modified final-block readouts, and released Dense Cosine Similarity Map (DCSM) scorers. At 224-pixel input resolution, a ClearCLIP-style readout increases proposal-based detection AP from 2.6 to 27.3 on 4,952 images, yet its mean-map scorer obtains 39.4% balanced spatial-selection accuracy, versus 50.3% for the ordinary readout. On 527 spatial queries from 375 images, released DCSM ObjA and COCO scorers reach 58.1% [53.7, 62.4] and 57.3% [53.2, 61.2], respectively, against 45.7% expected chance (exploratory percentile 95% image-cluster bootstrap intervals). These conditional, annotation-derived results motivate separate validation of localization and relational selection; they neither isolate a causal mechanism nor test learned DCSM scoring on modified features.
patches.new: We report a descriptive separation between category-sensitive localization and relational object selection in the evaluated CLIP pipelines. A map that highlights a category need not identify the intended instance among objects of that category. We analyze saved COCO experiments with a frozen ViT-B/16, ordinary and modified final-block readouts, and local Dense Cosine Similarity Map (DCSM) checkpoint-adapter pipelines. At 224-pixel input resolution, a ClearCLIP-style readout increases proposal-based detection AP from 2.6 to 27.3 on 4,952 images, yet its pooled-text map scorer obtains 39.4% balanced spatial-selection accuracy, versus 50.3% for the ordinary readout. On 527 spatial queries from 375 images, the local DCSM pipelines labeled ObjA and COCO reach 58.1% [53.7, 62.4] and 57.3% [53.2, 61.2], respectively, against 45.7% expected chance (exploratory percentile 95% image-cluster bootstrap intervals). Checkpoint release identities remain unverified. These conditional, annotation-derived results motivate separate validation of localization and relational selection; they neither isolate a causal mechanism nor test learned DCSM scoring on modified features.

patches.old: Two released DCSM checkpoints [@kang2025dcsm], locally called ObjA and COCO, score context crops using ordinary CLIP features and an already trained CNN. The adapter supplies an image-position-by-text-position matrix (197-by-30), including image CLS and text BOS/EOS/padding positions, with two convolutional layers and a 128-unit hidden fully connected layer. It inserts checkpoint functional embeddings using inherited whitespace positions and standardizes over all entries of the candidate-by-channel-by-image-position-by-text-position tensor for a query. Tokenizer alignment is not independently certified; normalization makes scores candidate-batch dependent. No new training is performed here, but these scorers are not training-free components. Modified readouts with the learned CNN were not evaluated. Local filenames and implementation provenance are recorded in the non-public supplement; checkpoint hashes and release versions remain unavailable.
patches.new: Two local DCSM checkpoint-adapter pipelines [@kang2025dcsm], labeled ObjA and COCO, score context crops using ordinary CLIP features and an already trained CNN. The adapter supplies an image-position-by-text-position matrix (197-by-30), including image CLS and text BOS/EOS/padding positions, to a scorer with two convolutional layers and a 128-unit hidden fully connected layer. The checkpoint functional embeddings correspond conceptually to the Functional Rows in the cited method; their local insertion uses inherited whitespace positions. The adapter standardizes over all entries of the candidate-by-channel-by-image-position-by-text-position tensor for a query. By contrast, the original method describes text-token rows, image-patch columns, EOS padding, and z-score normalization in its implementation appendix. These descriptions do not establish implementation equivalence: local tokenizer alignment and functional-position mapping are not independently certified, and the local normalization makes scores candidate-batch dependent. No new training is performed here, but these scorers are not training-free components. Modified readouts with the learned CNN were not evaluated. Local filenames and implementation provenance are recorded in the non-public supplement; verified checkpoint release identities, checkpoint hashes, release versions, and original execution revisions remain unavailable.
